items.title: Social Housing Bill receives Second Reading in the House of Commons
items.summary: As reported by the Chartered Institute of Housing, the Social Housing Bill receives its Second Reading in the House of Commons on 10 September 2026, having completed its Lords stages. The bill would reform the Right to Buy, require four weeks notice before a private registered provider sells a social home, and strengthen protections for tenants who are victims of domestic abuse.

items.title: PRS database opens for landlord registration from 15 December at 65 pounds per property
items.summary: As reported by the National Residential Landlords Association, registration on the new private rented sector database opens from 15 December 2026 in a 12-month rollout starting in the West Midlands. Landlords in England pay 65 pounds per property per year and must register all homes by 14 November 2027. Penalties run to 7,000 pounds, or 40,000 pounds for repeat breaches, and the Valuation Office is to take over section 13 rent increase challenges.

items.title: Regulator of Social Housing finds for-profit landlord failed governance and viability standards
items.summary: As reported by Housing Today, the Regulator of Social Housing found for-profit landlord Keystone CIC failed to meet governance and viability standards, after an investigation into weaknesses in its financial risk management and business planning. The Luton-based landlord plans to merge into another social landlord. Melton Borough Council was upgraded from C2 to C1 in the same batch.

items.title: Government calls for views on revising social housing allocations guidance
items.summary: As reported by Local Government Lawyer, the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government has called for evidence on the statutory guidance covering social housing allocations in England. It will consider qualification rules, local connection, affordability, debt and anti-social behaviour criteria, and how schemes affect homeless and vulnerable households. The current guidance dates from 2012.

items.title: Councils call for tighter rules on sale of social homes to non-resident buyers
items.summary: As reported by Housing Today, the Local Councils Network has urged the government to tighten the rules on sales of subsidised social and affordable homes to private buyers who do not live in them, after figures reached record levels. Research based on Freedom of Information requests found housing associations in England have sold roughly 25,000 such homes since 2018/19, including 5,250 in 2024/25.

items.title: MoJ evaluation reveals legal aid training grant success for housing sector
items.summary: As reported by Law Society Gazette, the Ministry of Justice has evaluated a 1.5 million pound grant that ran from 2023 to 2025 to recruit housing and debt solicitors. It helped train up to 31 solicitors across 26 provider firms, and 90 per cent said they could not have hired a trainee without it. The department is now considering next steps for the housing legal aid sector.

items.title: Scottish Government publishes Awaab's Law guidance for tenants in Scotland
items.summary: As reported by Scottish Government, Awaab's Law comes into force in Scotland on 6 October 2026, with earlier cases outside its timeframes. Landlords must investigate damp or mould reports within 10 working days, give written findings within 3, and begin repairs within 5. It applies to Scottish Secure, Short Scottish Secure and most private tenancies.

items.title: Foreign lawyer struck off after submitting AI-generated false case citations at the SDT
items.summary: As reported by Law Society Gazette, a foreign lawyer who used AI-generated false case citations in a written defence before the Solicitors Disciplinary Tribunal was struck off. The tribunal, considering such citations for the first time, warned it would take a hard line on lawyers misleading proceedings through AI. A reminder to housing disrepair specialists to verify case law sourced from AI.

items.title: RSH quarterly survey: repairs and maintenance spending across social housing reaches 9.7 billion pounds in 12 months
items.summary: As reported by GOV.UK, the Regulator of Social Housing's quarterly survey shows repairs and maintenance spend by private registered providers reached 2.4 billion pounds in the quarter to June 2026, totalling 9.7 billion pounds over the past 12 months. Providers raised 4.3 billion pounds in the quarter and forecast 11.1 billion pounds of repairs spend over the next year.

items.title: Thursday Housing Update 25: what happens when the estimated cost of repairs is wrong
items.summary: As reported by consultant lawyer Steve Cornforth, his weekly update for housing conditions practitioners discusses a claim reallocated from the Small Claims Track to the Fast Track after a defendant's estimated cost of repairs proved inaccurate at allocation. It also reviews when a landlord may obtain forced access for an inspection, drawing on the county court decision in Stonewater Ltd v Harris.

items.title: CIH and CIOB publish joint guidance on tackling damp and mould in social housing
items.summary: As reported by the Chartered Institute of Housing, it and the Chartered Institute of Building have jointly published guidance titled Tackling damp and mould: professional practice, cultural change and regulation in social housing. The guide reflects Awaab's Law and the Hazards in Social Housing (Prescribed Requirements) (England) Regulations 2025, and covers construction causes of damp and mould.

items.title: One in four young people use AI to help with their legal needs, Justice research finds
items.summary: As reported by Artificial Lawyer, research by the legal charity Justice and the Administrative Fairness Lab found that just over a quarter of 18 to 24 year olds used AI when facing a legal problem, against around 10% of those aged 55 to 64. Many turned to AI on problems largely outside legal aid, including housing, employment and debt, raising accuracy concerns about unregulated chatbot advice.
